title: Statistical delocalization in the Anyonic Aubry-André model
authors: Andoni Agirre, André Eckardt, Tobias Grass
abstract: Many-body localization is remarkable in that localization persists despite the presence of dynamical interactions. Here we demonstrate the converse phenomenon: enhanced many-body delocalization induced solely by exchange statistics. We study a Aubry-André quasiperiodic system of anyons in one dimension in the absence of density-density interactions. In terms of anyon operators, the system is described by a quadratic Hamiltonian. By analyzing the finite-size scaling of its spectral properties and the inverse participation ratio of many-body eigenstates, we find that increasing the anyonic statistical phase systematically shifts the many-body localization crossover toward larger quasiperdiodic potentials. We further confirm these findings using a dynamical probe, namely the persistence of an initial density imbalance following quenches. Our results establish exchange statistics as an independent mechanism capable of altering many-body localization, revealing a fundamentally distinct route to delocalization in one-dimensional quantum systems.
summary: This theoretical work explores how the inherent exchange statistics of anyons can drive many-body delocalization in a quasiperiodic 1D system, even in the absence of density-density interactions. By analyzing spectral properties and dynamics, the authors show that tuning the statistical phase $	heta$ systematically shifts the system's localization transition. This reveals that exchange statistics constitutes a fundamental, independent route to quantum delocalization in low-dimensional quantum matter.
main_problem: The study investigates enhanced many-body delocalization in quantum systems induced solely by the exchange statistics of anyons, contrasting with conventional many-body localization (MBL).
main_result: Increasing the anyonic statistical phase systematically shifts the many-body localization crossover toward larger quasiperiodic potentials, establishing exchange statistics as an independent mechanism for delocalization.
method: The analysis employs finite-size scaling of spectral properties (gap ratio) and the inverse participation ratio (IPR), supplemented by dynamical probes like monitoring density imbalance after quenches.
model_or_system: The system is an anyonic Aubry-André (AA) quasiperiodic model in one dimension, described by a quadratic Hamiltonian involving anyon operators $a_j$. The statistics are controlled by the phase angle $	heta$.
key_observables: Fractal dimension ($D_2$), Gap ratio ($r_k$), Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), and long-time density imbalances.
important_parameters: The statistical phase angle $	heta \in [0, 2\pi)$, the potential strength $V$, and the system filling $N/L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on finite-size scaling, which may not conclusively distinguish between a true phase transition and a crossover regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $D_2$ and the gap ratio on the potential strength $V$ for various $	heta$, and show the evolution of density imbalances over time for different statistical regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the localization transition using multiple diagnostics (spectral, IPR, dynamics) to map out how the statistical phase $	heta$ modifies the critical potential $V_c$ required for delocalization.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the interplay between particle statistics (anyons) and many-body dynamics, providing a novel, non-interaction-based mechanism to tune localization in 1D quantum systems, relevant to ultracold atomic simulations of exotic statistics.

figures.caption: Figure 1. (a,b) Fractal dimension D2 vs. AA potential strength V , at filling N = L (a) and filling L = 4N (b), for different values of θ. We obtain D2 from linear regression of −log IPR as a function of log D, at the available system sizes (see App. A). Error bars are obtained from stochastic resampling over a normal distribution of IPR values. (c,d) Gap ratio vs. V at filling one (L = 10), and at filling 1/4 (L = 20), for different values of θ. Error bars represent standard errors from ensemble averages.

Figure 2. (a–c) Raw data of η vs V at filling 1 for different N, considering θ values for bosons (θ = 0), weak anyons (θ = 0.1π), strong anyons (θ = 0.5π), and (e–g) the corresponding collapsed data after FSS. In panels (d) and (h), we illustrate, for the case of weak anyons, the FSS based on gap ratio r.

Figure 3. We plot the system parameters obtained from FSS with η and r, as a function of the statistical angle θ. In panels (a–c), we plot the critical potential strength Vc vs. θ. In panels (d–f), we plot the exponent ν vs. θ. Results at different fillings are shown: N/L = 1 in panels (a,d), N/L = 1/2 in panels (b,e), and N/L = 1/4 in panels (c,f). Error bars are the standard deviations after repeating FSS from resampling over 100 randomly generated distributions.

Figure 4. Left-right imbalance ILR(t) for a half-filled chain (L = 12, N = 6) following a quench from the fully imbalanced initial state in Eq. (6).Panels (a)–(d) correspond to bosons (θ = 0), weak anyons (θ = 0.1π), strong anyons (θ = 0.5π), and pseudofermions (θ = π), respectively. Different curves show different values of the Aubry-André potential strength V . Increasing the statistical angle systematically enhances the relaxation of the imbalance, indicating a shift of the localization crossover towards larger values of V .

Figure 5. Saturation imbalance analysis for filling 1/2 chains at different potential strengths. The saturation value of the LR imbalance ILR is shown as a function of the statistical angle θ for different system sizes for V = 4J (a) and V = 7J (c). Panels (b) and (d) show the saturation values of the imbalance plotted against 1/N for different θ values with V = 4J and V = 7J, respectively.
